reasons: No test file is visible in the packet, although test identifiers and a note about a deterministic check suggest one exists.
The size-scale code has unused variables (aMin and aMax) that are voided, which is dead code.
Export settings fall back silently when saved data is unreadable.

terms.meaning: A chart that places dots on two number scales, here schedule slip and cost overrun.
The size of a dot, scaled so that its area rather than its radius matches the value.
Capital expenditure, the money spent to build a project. Here, the realised value if known, otherwise the planned value.
How many years a project finished later than its plan.
A small save area in the web browser that keeps settings between visits.
The file format used by Microsoft PowerPoint presentations.
The most common unit of capacity among projects, used so that only comparable capacities are sized together.
A reusable piece of React logic, such as the saved-setting helper used here.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and chart rules
sections.what: Brings in the chart library, house colours and layout, the saved-setting helper, the data readers, and the bubble dimensions. The header comment states the chart rules.
sections.why: The header comment records the rules: plot only complete projects, label approximations, and never size a bubble from a capacity that is not known.
sections.watch_out: The constants MIN_R and MAX_R set the smallest and largest bubble size, so changing them alters every bubble on the slide.

sections.name: PlotPoint
sections.title: Shape of one plotted dot
sections.what: Defines the data each dot carries: name, label with an approximate marker, horizontal and vertical position, size, capacity unit, capex, country, approximation flag and note, and the colour category values.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the drawing code and the hover box working from one agreed format.
sections.watch_out: A missing field here means the hover box or colour code will show nothing for that item.

sections.name: plottable
sections.title: Deciding which projects get a dot
sections.what: Turns one project into a dot, or returns nothing when planned budget, actual budget, or schedule slip is missing, or when planned budget is zero or less. Converts slip from months to years and works out the percent overrun. Capex uses the actual value when it is positive, otherwise the planned value.
sections.why: The header says nothing is fabricated, so a project with missing figures is left out instead of guessed.
sections.watch_out: Dropped projects appear only in the lower n count, so a missing project is easy to overlook.

sections.name: niceFloor
sections.title: Rounding a reference size
sections.what: Rounds a number down to a tidy value (1, 2, or 5 times a power of ten). Used for the example bubble in the legend.
sections.why: Likely reason: the example value is easier to read when it is round.
sections.watch_out: Zero or negative input is returned unchanged, so the legend example would be odd in that case.

sections.name: paddedDomain
sections.title: Padding the chart edges
sections.what: Finds the lowest and highest values, always includes zero, and adds 10 percent of space at each edge. If all values are equal, it widens the range by one unit each way.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps dots away from the chart edges and handles charts where all values match.
sections.watch_out: An empty list gives a range around zero only, so callers should check for empty data first.

sections.name: BubbleSlideTooltip
sections.title: Hover box with approximate marking
sections.what: The hover box for one dot. Shows name, cost overrun, schedule slip, capacity, capex, and country. An approximate slip keeps its tilde, gets an approximate tag, and shows the stored assumption note.
sections.why: The comment says approximate values must be clearly labelled, and that this box is exported so checks can render it directly.
sections.watch_out: Changing the labels or test identifiers here breaks those checks.

sections.name: BubbleFilter (part 1)
sections.title: Filter dropdown for one category
sections.what: A button that opens a checklist of values for one category, with a count next to each. The button turns red and shows a number when any box is ticked.
sections.why: Lets readers narrow the chart by region, segment, or status.
sections.watch_out: Test identifiers are built from the option text, so renaming an option also changes the test identifiers.

sections.name: BubbleFilter (part 2)
sections.title: Closing the filter dropdown
sections.what: Ends the dropdown component. Contains no separate behaviour.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Structural only.

sections.name: BubbleSidebarContent, SlideSize, EMPTY_FILTERS
sections.title: Sidebar and size choice types
sections.what: Defines the optional sidebar title, banner, and item list. Defines the three size choices and the empty filter set.
sections.why: Lets a caller replace the sidebar text, and keeps size choices limited to three valid values.
sections.watch_out: A new size option must be added to this type and to the size buttons together.

sections.name: isFilterRecord
sections.title: Checking saved filter data
sections.what: Checks that saved filter settings contain a list of text values for each category.
sections.why: Likely reason: browser storage can hold old or damaged values, and this check stops them from breaking the slide.
sections.watch_out: A new category must be added to this check, or its saved choices are discarded.

sections.name: benchmarkChartKeys
sections.title: Storage names for each industry
sections.what: Builds the names used to save the size and filter choices, each including the industry slug so every industry keeps its own choices.
sections.why: The comment says these names are kept separate from the Analysis page names.
sections.watch_out: Changing the naming pattern silently forgets all saved choices.

sections.name: benchmarkChartExport
sections.title: Settings for the PowerPoint export
sections.what: Reads the saved size and filter choices for an industry, then returns the size, the IDs of projects that pass the filters, and a text note describing the active filters.
sections.why: The comment says this makes the exported slide match what is on screen.
sections.watch_out: If saved data cannot be read, it falls back to capacity sizing and no filters without warning, so the export can differ from the screen.

sections.name: SLIDE_SIZES
sections.title: Size button labels
sections.what: The three size options shown as buttons, each with its display name.
sections.why: Keeps the button order and names in one place.
sections.watch_out: The keys must match the size type exactly, or the selected button will not light up.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleSlide (part 1)
sections.title: Slide state and filtered dots
sections.what: Holds the colour category, the size choice, and the filters. Works out filter options with counts from the full project list, applies the filters, and turns the remaining projects into dots sized by the chosen mode. In capacity mode only the most common unit is sized.
sections.why: Likely reason: options come from the full list so choices do not vanish while filtering.
sections.watch_out: Filter options are built from all projects, but the dots come only from the filtered list, so counts and dots can differ on purpose.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleSlide (part 2)
sections.title: Legend, size scale and averages
sections.what: Builds the colour legend with counts, the size scale (bubble area proportional to value, with a 3 pixel minimum radius), the capacity unit label, the example size, and the counts of hollow and approximate dots. Also finds the largest overrun project and the averages and axis ranges.
sections.why: The comments say colours stay fixed when filtering and bubble area is kept proportional to value.
sections.watch_out: Zero or negative sizes are treated as missing and drawn as hollow markers.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleSlide (part 3)
sections.title: Drawing each bubble
sections.what: Draws each dot as a filled circle coloured by its category, or as a hollow dashed circle when its size is unknown. Adds a red ring around the largest overrun project and sets up the name label.
sections.why: The hollow marker keeps unknown capacity from looking like a known size.
sections.watch_out: Dots overlap, so the drawing order matters; the sort is done separately in a later section.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleSlide (part 4)
sections.title: Sidebar of notable projects
sections.what: Builds the default sidebar, listing cancelled, halted, or on-hold projects in the current selection with a count banner. A caller-supplied sidebar replaces it.
sections.why: The comment says the default is taken honestly from the filtered selection.
sections.watch_out: Projects that are cancelled but have no plottable data still appear in the sidebar and in the banner count.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleSlide (part 5)
sections.title: Colour, size and filter controls
sections.what: Draws the colour-by buttons, the size buttons, the filter dropdowns, and a clear-filters button shown when any filter is set.
sections.why: Lets readers change the view without leaving the slide.
sections.watch_out: The clear button resets three categories by name, so a new category must be added there too.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleSlide (part 6)
sections.title: Legend row and size note
sections.what: Shows the colour legend with counts, a key for hollow markers with their count, a count of approximate slips, and an example reference circle with its unit and an explanation of size.
sections.why: Explains the chart so the reader can read it without help.
sections.watch_out: The approximate-slip count depends on the stored approximation flag, so it is only as accurate as that data.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleSlide (part 7)
sections.title: Empty state and quadrant captions
sections.what: If nothing can be plotted, shows a message (different text when filters are the cause). Otherwise places four italic captions in the corners describing the quadrants.
sections.why: The captions tell readers how to interpret each area of the chart.
sections.watch_out: The caption wording is fixed, so it makes the same judgement on every chart whatever the data shows.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleSlide (part 8)
sections.title: Highlight of the worst-overrun project
sections.what: Shows a small box near the top right with the name, cost overrun, schedule slip, and any approximate note for the project with the highest cost overrun.
sections.why: Draws attention to the most extreme project from the data itself.
sections.watch_out: The box sits at a fixed position and can cover bubbles, and when two projects tie, the first one in the list is chosen.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleSlide (part 9)
sections.title: Chart axes and average lines
sections.what: Creates the chart area with a grid, labelled horizontal and vertical axes, and dashed grey average lines with labels.
sections.why: The averages give readers a benchmark to compare each project against.
sections.watch_out: The averages are plain means of the plotted points, so a few extreme projects can pull them far from the typical value.

sections.name: CostScheduleBubbleSlide (part 10)
sections.title: Hover box, bubbles and sidebar layout
sections.what: Connects the hover box, draws the bubbles largest first so small ones stay visible on top, and places the sidebar panel with its title, banner, and list, or an empty message.
sections.why: Likely reason: drawing large bubbles first stops them from hiding small ones.
sections.watch_out: The sort is made on a copy, so removing it would hide small bubbles under large ones.

summary: Draws the House-style cost-versus-schedule bubble slide for a Benchmark Scan, with filters, size choices, averages, a highlighted worst-overrun project, and a sidebar of cancelled, halted, or on-hold projects.
purpose: Lets a reader see, for a group of capital projects, how far cost overran plan and how far schedule slipped, with bubble size and colour chosen by the reader.
why: The header comment says only projects with planned budget, actual budget, and a schedule slip are plotted, and that nothing is invented to fill the chart. Approximate slips are labelled, so estimates are never shown as exact.
how: 1. Take the projects in the report data. 2. Keep only those that match the active filters. 3. Turn each project into a point with schedule slip in years and cost overrun in percent, dropping projects with missing figures. 4. Size each point by equal size, capex, or capacity, using only the most common capacity unit for capacity mode. 5. Work out the averages, the largest overrun, and the axis ranges. 6. Draw the frame, controls, legend, quadrant captions, chart, and sidebar. The export helper reads the same saved settings so the PowerPoint output matches the screen.
inputs: The slide context (`ctx`) with the report data (`data.projects`), industry name, industry slug, and page number. Optional sidebar text overrides. Saved size and filter choices in browser storage, under keys made by `benchmarkChartKeys`.
outputs: A slide element inside the House frame. Also `benchmarkChartExport`, which returns the size choice, the IDs of projects that pass the filters, and a text note describing the active filters.
risks: Projects missing planned budget, actual budget, or schedule slip are dropped silently, apart from the lower count shown as n. Capacity bubbles compare only one unit. The export falls back to capacity sizing and no filters if saved data cannot be read, so an export can differ from the screen without warning. Quadrant captions are fixed wording and assume that further right and higher mean worse.
debug: If the chart is empty, check the n value in the header and the empty-state message, then confirm the projects have planned budget, actual budget, and a schedule slip. If bubbles look unsized, check that projects share a capacity unit. If filters look wrong, inspect the browser storage keys that start with benchmark-scan-bubble. If the export differs from the screen, check `benchmarkChartExport` and the saved values it reads.
